topic: sort() mutates in place and returns the same array: use toSorted()
text:
Your list sorted fine. Then the original array changed too. 🤔

Array.prototype.sort() sorts in place and returns a reference to the same array. MDN says it plainly: "no copy is made".

const sorted = users.sort(byName);
sorted === users; // true

In React, that means sorting props or state quietly mutates data other components also read.

The fix is one word: toSorted() returns a new array and leaves the original alone. It's been available across browsers since July 2023.

const sorted = users.toSorted(byName);
sorted === users; // false

My rule of thumb: in UI code, reach for toSorted() by default. Use sort() only on an array you just created yourself.

Have you ever chased a bug that turned out to be a mutating array method?
